items.stem: Which description matches how a recurrent network reads a sentence?

options.text: It reads one word at a time and rewrites a fixed-size note each time.
options.feedback: The note is the hidden state. Each step takes the previous note and the next word and produces a new note.

options.text: It keeps every word and compares each word with all the others.
options.feedback: That describes attention, a later design. A recurrent network keeps only the note.

options.text: It reads the whole sentence at once and picks out the keywords from it.
options.feedback: A recurrent network cannot read ahead. It reads in order, one word at a time.

options.text: It looks up each word in a table of meanings and joins the results.
options.feedback: There is no table of meanings. The note is a list of numbers that the model updates.

items.stem: A recurrent model has read "The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired" and is asked what "it" refers to. Which noun is stronger on the note?

options.text: Street, because it was read more recently.
options.feedback: Each new word makes the older words weaker, so the later noun is stronger.

options.text: Animal, because it is the subject of the sentence.
options.feedback: The note tracks no grammar. It holds weaker traces of earlier words.

options.text: Both equally, because the sentence is short.
options.feedback: The note fades earlier words at every step, even in a short sentence.

options.text: Neither, because nouns are dropped from the note.
options.feedback: All words are written onto the note, and the older ones are weaker.

items.stem: You switch the sentence from "too tired" to "too wide", and the model still answers "street". What does this show?

options.text: The answer follows how recently each noun was read, and the last word has no effect.
options.feedback: The note holds street more strongly in both sentences, so the answer is the same. Meaning played no part.

options.text: The model understood that streets can be wide, so it chose correctly.
options.feedback: It gave the same answer for "tired", where street is wrong. A model that used meaning would change its answer.

options.text: The model ran out of memory and fell back on the last noun it read.
options.feedback: The note is always the same size, so it never runs out.

options.text: The model guesses at random between the two nouns each time.
options.feedback: The strengths on the note fix the choice, so it is the same every time.

items.stem: An older recurrent model reads a 50-page contract. Which problems should you expect?

options.text: Early details are weak on the note, and training is slow because words are read in order.
options.feedback: These are the two problems of distance and order.

options.text: It refuses to read more than 50 words, because the note has no room for more.
options.feedback: There is no word limit. The weakness is that old content fades.

options.text: It remembers the first page best, because it was the first thing it read.
options.feedback: The note keeps the newest words strongest and older words weaker.

options.text: It reads all pages at once, which makes it very expensive to run.
options.feedback: A recurrent model reads in order. Reading everything at once is what attention does.
